questions.question: What is the time complexity of accessing an element in an array by index?
questions.explanation: Arrays store elements contiguously in memory. The address of any element is computed as base + index × size, so it's always one step regardless of array length.

incorrect_explanations.O(log n): That's binary search — requires the array to be sorted and does repeated halving.
incorrect_explanations.O(n): That's linear scan — you'd need to check every element.
incorrect_explanations.O(n²): That would be something like a nested loop over all pairs.

questions.question: Why does using a hash map reduce Two Sum from O(n²) to O(n)?
options: Because hash maps sort the array automatically
Because each lookup is O(1), so we do n lookups instead of n² comparisons
Because hash maps use binary search internally
Because we only iterate once and skip duplicates
questions.answer: Because each lookup is O(1), so we do n lookups instead of n² comparisons
questions.explanation: With a nested loop you compare every pair — that's n*(n-1)/2 operations. A hash map lets you check 'have I seen the complement?' in O(1), so one pass through n elements gives O(n) total.

incorrect_explanations.Because hash maps sort the array automat: Hash maps don't sort — they provide O(1) average lookup by key.
incorrect_explanations.Because hash maps use binary search inte: Hash maps use hashing, not binary search. Binary search requires sorted data.
incorrect_explanations.Because we only iterate once and skip du: We do iterate once, but skipping duplicates isn't the reason — it's the O(1) lookup.
